desc:
Backup and disaster recovery setup protects your files, databases and settings with automatic copies and a restore that has been proven to work. Ecom Swift LLC builds the schedule, stores the copies safely and writes the recovery steps down.

## What is backup and disaster recovery?

Backup and disaster recovery is the combination of two things: regular copies of your data, and a clear plan for putting those copies back when something breaks. The backup is the insurance policy. The recovery plan is the claim process. Having only the first leaves you guessing at the worst possible moment.

Most small teams have some kind of backup, often a server snapshot or a checkbox their host turned on years ago. Few have ever restored from it. Until a restore has been done once, nobody knows whether the copy is complete, how long it takes or who has the right to start it.

## Why untested backups fail

Backups fail quietly. A disk fills up, a password changes, a new database is added and never included, or the job stops running after an update. Nothing warns you, and the gap appears only when you need the data.

Recovery also fails for human reasons. The person who set everything up has left, the login is in an old email, or nobody agrees on what to restore first. A short written order of steps removes the argument and the panic. It also shortens the outage, because the team spends its time restoring instead of searching.

## How good recovery protects your business

Good recovery limits two things: how much data you can lose and how long you are offline. These are often called the recovery point and the recovery time. A shop that loses a day of orders or a web app that stays down for a morning feels both as lost trust, support tickets and manual rework.

Backups also cover mistakes that have nothing to do with outages. An employee deletes a table, a bad release overwrites content, or ransomware encrypts a server. In each case a clean older copy, stored somewhere the attacker or the mistake cannot reach, is what turns a crisis into a task.

## What a dependable backup setup includes

- A list of everything that matters: application files, databases, uploaded media, configuration and secrets.
- Automatic backups on a schedule that fits how often your data changes.
- A retention rule that keeps recent copies and older ones without filling your storage.
- A second storage location, separate from the account or region that holds the live system.
- Encryption of copies, so a stolen backup is not a readable one.
- Alerts that tell a named person when a backup fails or is skipped.
- A real restore into a clean environment, checked by opening the app and reading the data.
- Written recovery steps with owners, order of work and who to contact.
- Recovery time and data-loss targets agreed in plain words.
- A reminder to repeat the restore test on a regular schedule.

## How we set it up

We start by listing your systems and asking what you could not afford to lose. From that list we configure automated backups for each system using the tools your cloud or host already provides, adding scripts only where they are needed. Copies are stored in your own storage account, so you keep control of them.

Next we run a real restore, not just a check that files exist. We bring the data back into a separate environment, confirm the application starts and note how long each step took. Those timings feed the one-page recovery guide.

The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in how many systems are covered, whether copies go to a second location, how much alerting is added and whether a full practice recovery run and team walkthrough are included.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Back up databases, uploads and configuration, not only code.
- Keep one copy outside the account that runs the live system.
- Restore a copy on a schedule and record what happened.
- Decide who is allowed to start a recovery before it is needed.
- Store the recovery guide somewhere that does not depend on the broken system.

**Avoid:**
- Treating a server snapshot as the entire plan.
- Keeping backups on the same disk as the data they protect.
- Assuming a green status light means a usable copy.
- Letting backup credentials sit unchanged when staff leave.
- Waiting for an incident to find out how long recovery takes.

## Who this is for

This service suits a small online business whose only copy of its orders sits in one database. It suits an agency that hosts client sites and needs proof it can restore them. It also suits a startup preparing for a customer security questionnaire that asks how data is protected and recovered.

## What we need from you

Send a short list of the apps, databases and storage you use, plus the name of your cloud or hosting provider. Tell us roughly how much downtime or lost data your business could tolerate. We never need your passwords. Access is given to us as a collaborator, team member or limited developer user in your own account, and you can remove it whenever the work is done.
